findings.summary: Unknown event signers could self-enroll using event-supplied public keys.
findings.resolution: Unknown signers now fail closed after the narrowly scoped operator-genesis bootstrap; additional devices require an already-authorized DeviceEnrolled event.

findings.summary: A public constructor could start the full loopback TCP API without authentication.
findings.resolution: Unauthenticated TCP constructors and serving helpers were removed; every TCP service now requires a private file-backed bearer token.

findings.summary: Unknown-signed conflict losers and conflict-resolution events could bypass folded-state signer checks.
findings.resolution: The complete causal stream is now authorized against the accumulated device registry before conflict selection, resolution, frontier advancement, or persistence of imported updates.

findings.summary: Imported device-management events relied on a self-declared operator actor kind.
findings.resolution: Folded state now binds operator authority to the genesis signing key and transfers it only through an authorized key rotation; operator events must be signed by a currently active operator key.

findings.summary: Unsigned schema-v1 events could bypass the new Loro authorization prepass.
findings.resolution: Project Loro ingestion and imports now reject every non-v2 event before causal or conflict processing; legacy v1 history remains available only through the explicit backed-up journal migration path.

findings.summary: Reinstalling an equivalent hook bundle as a new signed generation advanced current but left the bundle index on the prior generation.
findings.resolution: Activation and rollback now preflight bundle collisions and publish the verified runtime/index before moving current. Repointing a same-ID bundle is allowed only after proving identical signed dispatcher bytes; a regression fixture covers install and rollback.

findings.summary: An intermediate fix moved current before publishing a new bundle index, creating a hook-resolution crash window.
findings.resolution: The final ordering publishes and verifies the bundle runtime first, then atomically advances current. A same-ID repoint cannot change hook behavior because collision validation requires identical signed dispatcher bytes.
